```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
theme_set(theme_bw(18))
set.seed(222)

# Distribution of intensification
x_mean <- 80
x_disp <- 0.2
x_shape <- 1 / x_disp
x_rate <- 1 / (x_mean * x_disp)

yield_change <- rgamma(200, x_shape, x_rate) - 40

# make indigenous stewardship inversely correlated with yield change
indigenous_steward <- rbinom(200, size = 1, prob = plogis(-yield_change / 50))

# forest_loss = beta_0 + beta_1 * yield_change + beta_2 * indig_steward + beta_3 * yield_change * indig_steward

beta_0 <- -5
beta_1 <- -0.08
beta_2 <- 2
beta_3 <- 0.1
sigma <- 3

forest_data <- tibble(
  yield_change,
  indigenous_steward,
  indigenous_steward_fct = factor(indigenous_steward, labels = c("No", "Yes")),
  mu = beta_0 +
    beta_1 * yield_change +
    beta_2 * indigenous_steward +
    beta_3 * yield_change * indigenous_steward,
  forest_loss = -rnorm(200, mu, sigma)
)
```

# Interactions

## Learning objectives

- **Recognize** interactive terms
- **Model** regressions with interactions
- **Compare** interactive models to additive

# Recognize interactive terms

## Recall multiple regression


::: {.columns}

::: {.column style="font-size: 0.8em; width: 40%"}

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (x_2=B) + \epsilon \\
\epsilon &\sim Normal(0, \sigma)
\end{align}
$$

:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
expand_grid(x2 = c("A", "B"), x1 = c(0, 10)) |>
  mutate(y = 2 - 4 * (x2 == "B") + 1.5 * x1) |>
  ggplot(aes(x1, y, linetype = x2)) +
  geom_line() +
  expand_limits(y = 0)
```

:::

:::

Each predictor ($x_1$, $x_2=B$) has it's own coefficient ($\beta_1$, $\beta_2$). They act on $y$ separately.

## Interactions mediate relationships

In regular multiple regression, the _relationship_ between $x_1$ and $y$ is the same regardless of $x_2$.

But what if the _relationship_ between $x_1$ and $y$ varies with $x_2$?


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

```{r}
expand_grid(x2 = c("A", "B"), x1 = c(0, 10)) |>
  mutate(y = 2 - 4 * (x2 == "B") + 1.5 * x1) |>
  ggplot(aes(x1, y, linetype = x2)) +
  geom_line() +
  expand_limits(y = 0)
```

:::

::: {.column}

```{r}
expand_grid(x2 = c("A", "B"), x1 = c(0, 10)) |>
  mutate(y = 2 - 4 * (x2 == "B") + 1.5 * x1 - 2 * x1 * (x2 == "B")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x1, y, linetype = x2)) +
  geom_line() +
  expand_limits(y = 0)
```

:::

:::

## Deforestation and agriculture

::: {.columns style="font-size: 0.8em"}

::: {.column}

**Land sparing hypothesis**

Increasing yields _reduces_ deforestation.

:::

::: {.column}

**Rebound hypothesis**

Increasing yields _incentivizes_ deforestation.

:::

:::

![A section of the Amazon rainforest stands next to soy fields in Belterra, Para state, Brazil, on Nov. 30, 2019. (AP Photo/Leo Correa, File)](https://dims.apnews.com/dims4/default/b390455/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5379x3584+0+0/resize/980x653!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.apnews.com%2Fa8%2Fb3%2Fd98d7f6d398774758484cd6495ea%2F94701eddec5648c485e7c1627bbe5843)

## Two hypotheses

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em"}
What's the _relationship_ between deforestation and increasing yields? 
:::

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-align: center

expand_grid(yield = c(0, 10), hypothesis = c("Land sparing", "Rebound")) |>
     mutate(
          deforestation = ifelse(
               hypothesis == "Land sparing",
               8 - 0.6 * yield,
               2 + 0.6 * yield
          )
     ) |>
     ggplot(aes(yield, deforestation, color = hypothesis)) +
     geom_line(linewidth = 2, linetype = "dashed") +
     expand_limits(y = 0) +
     labs(
          x = "Yield change",
          y = "Deforestation rate",
          color = "Hypothesis"
     ) +
     theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
```

## Which hypothesis is supported?

Increasing yields increases deforestation: **rebound hypothesis**

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(forest_data, aes(yield_change, forest_loss)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "cornflowerblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Yield change (%)",
    y = "Deforestation rate (ha yr^-1)",
    caption = "Simulated data"
  )
```

## Does the _relationship_ vary?

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(
  forest_data,
  aes(yield_change, forest_loss, color = indigenous_steward_fct)
) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cornflowerblue", "firebrick")) +
  labs(
    x = "Yield change (%)",
    y = "Deforestation rate (ha yr^-1)",
    color = "Indigenous stewardship",
    caption = "Simulated data"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

# Model regressions with interactions

## Interactive terms

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_1 x_2 + \epsilon \\
\epsilon &\sim Normal(0, \sigma)
\end{align} 
$$

An interaction term **multiplies two predictors together**

## Deforestation and agriculture model

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} \\
&\quad + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times \text{Indig. Steward} + \epsilon \\
\epsilon &\sim Normal(0, \sigma)
\end{align} 
$$

What's the _relationship_ between deforestion and yield across groups?

## Interactions vary slopes

**No indigenous stewardship** 

$\text{Indig. Steward} = 0$

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} \\
&\quad + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times \text{Indig. Steward} \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 0 + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times 0 \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield}
\end{align} 
$$

::: {.fragment}

The slope is $\beta_1$

:::

## Interactions vary slopes

**Yes indigenous stewardship**

$\text{Indig. Steward} = 1$

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} \\
&\quad + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times \text{Indig. Steward} \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 1 + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times 1 \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \left( \beta_1 + \beta_3 \right) \text{Yield}
\end{align} 
$$


::: {.fragment}

The slope is $\beta_1 + \beta_3$

:::

## Interactions vary slopes

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-align: center

interaction_mod <- lm(
  forest_loss ~ yield_change * indigenous_steward,
  forest_data
)
coefs <- coef(interaction_mod)

# Prediction lines for each group
pred_lines <- tibble(
  indigenous_steward_fct = factor(c("No", "Yes"), levels = c("No", "Yes")),
  intercept = c(coefs[1], coefs[1] + coefs[3]),
  slope = c(coefs[2], coefs[2] + coefs[4])
)

# Fix panel limits and aspect ratio so labels can be rotated parallel to lines
pad <- function(r) r + c(-1, 1) * 0.05 * diff(r)
x_lim <- pad(range(forest_data$yield_change))
y_lim <- pad(range(forest_data$forest_loss))
aspect <- 0.6

slope_labels <- pred_lines %>%
  mutate(
    label = c("beta[1]", "beta[1] + beta[3]"),
    x = x_lim[1] + c(0.78, 0.75) * diff(x_lim),
    y = intercept + slope * x,
    angle = atan(slope * diff(x_lim) / diff(y_lim) * aspect) * 180 / pi
  )

ggplot(
  forest_data,
  aes(yield_change, forest_loss, color = indigenous_steward_fct)
) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_abline(
    aes(intercept = intercept, slope = slope, color = indigenous_steward_fct),
    pred_lines,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x, y, label = label, angle = angle),
    slope_labels,
    parse = TRUE,
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 7,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cornflowerblue", "firebrick")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = x_lim, ylim = y_lim, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Yield change (%)",
    y = "Deforestation rate (ha yr^-1)",
    color = "Indigenous stewardship",
    caption = "Simulated data"
  ) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = aspect,
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

# Compare interactive models to additive

## Additive vs. interactive

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}

**Additive**

$$
\text{Deforestation} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} + \epsilon
$$

**Interactive**

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} \\
&\quad + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times \text{Indig. Steward} + \epsilon
\end{align}
$$

:::

The only difference is the **interaction term**, $\beta_3 \text{Yield} \times \text{Indig. Steward}$

## Additive model: slope

**Yes indigenous stewardship**

$\text{Indig. Steward} = 1$

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 1 \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \beta_1 \text{Yield}
\end{align}
$$

::: {.fragment}

The slope is $\beta_1$, **the same as the no stewardship group**. Only the intercept changes.

:::

## Interactive model: slope

**Yes indigenous stewardship**

$\text{Indig. Steward} = 1$

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Deforestation} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Yield} + \beta_2 \text{Indig. Steward} \\
&\quad + \beta_3 \text{Yield} \times \text{Indig. Steward} \\
\text{Deforestation} &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \left( \beta_1 + \beta_3 \right) \text{Yield}
\end{align}
$$

::: {.fragment}

The slope is $\beta_1 + \beta_3$, **different from the no stewardship group**. Both the intercept and slope change.

:::

## Additive vs. interactive

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-align: center

additive_mod <- lm(
  forest_loss ~ yield_change + indigenous_steward,
  forest_data
)
add_coefs <- coef(additive_mod)

model_lines <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    model = "Additive",
    indigenous_steward_fct = factor(c("No", "Yes"), levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    intercept = c(add_coefs[1], add_coefs[1] + add_coefs[3]),
    slope = c(add_coefs[2], add_coefs[2])
  ),
  mutate(pred_lines, model = "Interactive")
)

forest_data |>
  cross_join(tibble(model = c("Additive", "Interactive"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(yield_change, forest_loss, color = indigenous_steward_fct)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_abline(
    aes(intercept = intercept, slope = slope, color = indigenous_steward_fct),
    model_lines,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cornflowerblue", "firebrick")) +
  labs(
    x = "Yield change (%)",
    y = "Deforestation rate (ha yr^-1)",
    color = "Indigenous stewardship",
    caption = "Simulated data"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}
The additive model forces parallel lines. It misses that stewardship removes the rebound effect.
:::

## When to use interactions

::: {.columns style="font-size: 0.9em"}

::: {.column}

**Additive**

Each predictor affects the response _independently_.

$x_2$ shifts $y$ up or down, but the effect of $x_1$ on $y$ is the same.

:::

::: {.column}

**Interactive**

One predictor _changes the effect_ of another on the response.

The effect of $x_1$ on $y$ depends on $x_2$.

:::

:::

::: {.fragment}

Ask: "Does the _relationship_ between $x_1$ and $y$ depend on $x_2$?"

:::

## Additive is sufficient

::: {.columns}

::: {.column style="font-size: 0.8em; width: 40%"}

**Snowpack and elevation**

North-facing slopes hold more snow than south-facing slopes at every elevation.

But snowpack increases with elevation at the same rate on both.

Aspect shifts the line; it doesn't change the slope.

:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
expand_grid(aspect = c("North", "South"), elevation = c(1500, 3000)) |>
  mutate(snowpack = -100 + 0.1 * elevation - 60 * (aspect == "South")) |>
  ggplot(aes(elevation, snowpack, color = aspect)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cornflowerblue", "firebrick")) +
  labs(
    x = "Elevation (m)",
    y = "Snow water equivalent (cm)",
    color = "Aspect"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

:::

:::

## Interactive is necessary

::: {.columns}

::: {.column style="font-size: 0.8em; width: 40%"}

**Stream and air temperature**

Streams warm as air temperature rises.

But a riparian canopy shades the stream, so shaded streams warm _more slowly_.

Canopy changes the slope of the relationship.

:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
expand_grid(canopy = c("Open", "Shaded"), air_temp = c(10, 30)) |>
  mutate(
    stream_temp = 4 +
      0.7 * air_temp -
      0.4 * air_temp * (canopy == "Shaded") +
      2 * (canopy == "Shaded")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(air_temp, stream_temp, color = canopy)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("firebrick", "cornflowerblue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Air temperature (°C)",
    y = "Stream temperature (°C)",
    color = "Riparian canopy"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

:::

:::
